bull.b: The operating qualification line provides tangible evidence that Westwater can produce and test battery-grade material against demanding customer specifications. This capability supports customer adoption, improves process readiness, and creates a stronger foundation for commercial sales when Kellyton commissioning advances.

Linking the Coosa resource with the nearby Kellyton processing plant gives Westwater a differentiated domestic mine-to-market model. If executed, this integration could improve supply security for U.S. battery customers and provide an early positioning advantage versus North American competitors.

Eliminating convertible debt reduces refinancing obligations, interest-related pressure, and balance-sheet complexity while the project is being developed. A largely unlevered structure preserves more flexibility to direct future capital toward construction, commissioning, and operational readiness.

bear.b: Westwater has not yet demonstrated operating scale or recurring customer revenue, leaving the business dependent on project execution before it can become self-funding. Persistent losses also reduce financial resilience and make future profitability dependent on successful plant commissioning and commercialization.

The remaining capital requirement is material relative to the company's pre-revenue status and limited cash generation. Securing additional financing is therefore central to completing equipment installation and commissioning, while delays or less favorable funding could slow the path to commercial operations.

Key elements of the growth strategy remain conditional rather than complete: Coosa still requires permitting progress, and the new anode product needs broader customer validation. These unresolved milestones can defer expansion, delay commercial acceptance, and extend the period before the platform reaches full potential.
